riposte: combined randomization-based tests across outcome representations

Source: R/riposte-package.R
riposte-package.Rd

riposte provides tests of the sharp null that combine several representations of an outcome to detect treatment effects a difference of means misses, in completely randomized, block-randomized, and cluster-randomized experiments. By default, p-values use direct re-randomization under the specified design. For unadjusted quadratic and Cauchy tests, users can instead choose engine = "asymptotic" to calculate p-values with chi-square and Cauchy approximations. See riposte_test().

Details

The three combinations are:

  • the quadratic (energy/distance) omnibus, which uses the full permutation covariance of the representations;

  • the Cauchy combination, which uses only each representation's marginal calibration; and

  • the max combination.

With the permutation engine, a screen chooses between the quadratic and the Cauchy from the conditioning of the permutation covariance, an ancillary quantity (a function of the outcomes under the sharp null and the design, not of the realized assignment).
